cat.name: Tools
cat.desc: Projects which serve some purpose, or act like it.

item.name: wisdomkey
item.desc: Small accessiblity program for moving around the mouse using a small set of keys.

item.name: Cesp
item.desc: A cross-editor live-share protocol I've helped my friend with. It works decently well, and does so in Emacs and Neovim!

item.name: kpedu
item.desc: A simple terminal-based text-editor with Emacs-like keybindings. You should probably just use Emacs though.

cat.name: Programming languages
cat.desc: Some toy languages I've made for fun. If my Github contributions are private for a long period of time, I've probably started working on a new one :) (that or I'm doing something actually reasonable)

item.name: Runtime
item.desc: A high-level, questionably-evaluated, interpreted programming language. Made for fun, and is not particularly efficient, but hopefully a bit fun to mess around with :)

item.name: Re-time
item.desc: A simple, purely object-oriented, Lisp inspired programming language which is a redesigned and rewritten version of Runtime. Same disclaimer as with Runtime, except I know even less about Haskell than C++.

cat.name: Web
cat.desc: Some small web projects I've made.

item.name: Wisdurm.fi
item.desc: This is my website, the one you're currently on!

item.name: Infinite canvas
item.desc: This is an (incomplete!) website that features a canvas for drawing, with infinite space to pan and zoom around in. Code for smoothing the lines and a possible shared canvas are in the works (circa 1846).

item.name: Rhythm game
item.desc: A simple rhythm game which uses MIDI-data to generate gameplay. Maybe doesn't work very well for complex songs, but still kinda cool! Heads up! These use DFJK for the control scheme!

item.name: Rhythm slop
item.desc: A very small & simple rhythm game, without any actual rhythm. I made this while bored at school. Heads up! These use DFJK for the control scheme!

cat.name: Games
cat.desc: Games I've that are more in depth experiences. This doesn't include all of my games, and even so these are all currently unfinished, but maybe you'll still find them cool. Most of these are also a pita to run since they were built with C# and SDL2 in Visual Studio.

item.name: Unnamed-Tower-Defense-Game
item.desc: This is a tower defense game I wrote in C#. It's currently in a perfectly playable state, but it's obviously unfinished. May be rewritten later.

item.name: Horrible World
item.desc: This is a war/civilization simulation game I also wrote in C#. This is, I believe, still my largest project by lines of code. (not that that's a good metric). Unfinished C++ rewrite also exists.

item.name: Terrabit
item.desc: Very simple text-based Terraria remake. More of a proof of concept, never got far into development. (Also my first proper programming project ever!). Probably won't be rewritten (but who knows!)

cat.name: Miscellaneous
cat.desc: Projects I've made that don't neatly fit into any of the other categories. These may be better organized in the future.

item.name: Desktop Flashbang
item.desc: What it says on the tin, a program which throws a flashbang on your screen.
